blocks.content: The grain wholesaler purchases and sells several groups of grain lots.

stem.prompt: Calculate the overall percentage gain or loss.

explanation.opening: Each purchase lot has its own quantity, unit cost and unit selling price, so the lots must be totalled in rupees.
explanation.concept: Overall percentage comes from the combined profit or loss amount divided by the combined cost of every lot.

steps.title: Total each lot separately
steps.body: Multiply quantity by unit cost and unit selling price for every listed lot.

steps.title: Combine the lot ledgers
steps.body: Add all lot costs and all lot receipts into two chapter-wide totals.

steps.title: Measure the combined rate
steps.body: Compare total receipt with total cost and divide the absolute difference by total cost.

explanation.conclusion: The sign of total receipt minus total cost gives the direction, and the ratio gives the overall percentage.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not average the individual lot percentages; quantities and unit costs create unequal money weights.

PNL-QL-071.difficultyRationale: Two linked calculations are required, but the reasoning path is directly visible.

blocks.content: A fruit merchant sells two fruit crates for the same price of ₹{commonSellingPrice} each. The first is sold at {firstRatePercent}% {firstDirection}, while the second is sold at {secondRatePercent}% {secondDirection}.

stem.prompt: Calculate the overall profit or loss percentage on the two crates together.

explanation.opening: The two selling prices are equal, but the cost prices are different because the profit and loss rates differ.
explanation.concept: Recover each cost price from the common selling price, add the costs, and compare them with the two equal selling amounts.

steps.title: Recover the first cost
steps.body: Reverse the first profit or loss multiplier from the common selling price.

steps.title: Recover the second cost
steps.body: Reverse the second multiplier in the same way.

steps.title: Combine both transactions
steps.body: Compare twice the common selling price with the sum of the two recovered costs.

explanation.conclusion: The combined comparison gives the overall profit or loss percentage.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not assume equal selling prices mean equal cost prices or that opposite rates cancel.

PNL-QL-072.difficultyRationale: A reverse step, base conversion, or two-stage commercial transformation is required.

blocks.content: An equipment dealer buys two small machines for the same cost of ₹{commonCostPrice} each. The first is sold at {firstRatePercent}% {firstDirection}, while the second is sold at {secondRatePercent}% {secondDirection}.

stem.prompt: Find the overall profit or loss percentage.

explanation.opening: Because both articles have the same cost price, their profit and loss amounts can be combined on equal bases.
explanation.concept: Use one convenient common cost, calculate both selling prices, and compare their total with twice the common cost.

steps.title: Choose a common cost base
steps.body: Take each cost price as the same convenient amount.

steps.title: Apply both rates
steps.body: Find the two selling-price factors from the stated directions.

steps.title: Combine the results
steps.body: Compare the sum of selling prices with the sum of costs.

explanation.conclusion: The combined difference on total cost is the overall percentage result.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not average signed rates when the question asks for a money-weighted overall result, even though equal costs make the arithmetic simpler.

PNL-QL-073.difficultyRationale: Two linked calculations are required, but the reasoning path is directly visible.

blocks.content: A retailer buys {totalQuantity} identical units at ₹{unitCostPrice} each.
{unsoldQuantity} units remain and recover ₹{unsoldRecoveryPerUnit} per unit.

stem.prompt: Calculate the overall percentage gain or loss on the complete inventory.

explanation.opening: A partial-inventory question becomes manageable when every sold and unsold group is entered in one money ledger.
explanation.concept: Total cost covers the entire stock, while total recovery includes receipts from sold groups plus any value recovered from remaining stock.

steps.title: Find total inventory cost
steps.body: Multiply total quantity by unit cost price.

steps.title: Add all recoveries
steps.body: Calculate revenue for every sold group and include the stated recovery from unsold units.

steps.title: Measure the overall result
steps.body: Compare total recovery with total cost and use total cost as the percentage base.

explanation.conclusion: The final comparison gives the overall profit or loss percentage for the complete inventory.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not ignore unsold or recovered stock when calculating the overall result.

blocks.content: A homeware seller buys {totalQuantity} ceramic sets at ₹{unitCostPrice} each. Of these, {damagedQuantity} sets are damaged and recover ₹{damagedRecoveryPerUnit} each. The seller wants an overall {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}.

stem.prompt: Find the required selling price per undamaged set.

explanation.opening: Damaged units have a fixed recovery, so the undamaged units must supply the rest of the target receipt.
explanation.concept: The target applies to the cost of the entire purchase, including the damaged units, before their recovery is deducted.

steps.title: Set the full-stock target
steps.body: Multiply total inventory cost by the required profit or loss factor.

steps.title: Credit damaged-stock recovery
steps.body: Subtract the amount recovered from damaged units from the target receipt.

steps.title: Price the undamaged units
steps.body: Divide the remaining receipt by the number of good units available for sale.

explanation.conclusion: The quotient is the selling price required for each undamaged unit.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not calculate the target only on good units; damaged units were part of the original cost.

PNL-QL-075.difficultyRationale: The unknown is coupled to several constraints, weighted groups, eligibility rules, or data-sufficiency logic.

blocks.content: A wholesaler pays for {paidQuantity} packaged units at ₹{unitCostPrice} each and receives {freeQuantity} additional units free. All units are sold at ₹{unitSellingPrice} each.

stem.prompt: Calculate the overall profit or loss percentage.

explanation.opening: Free units increase the number of units available for sale without increasing the purchase payment.
explanation.concept: Total cost is based only on paid units, while total revenue comes from all paid and free units that are sold.

steps.title: Find total acquisition cost
steps.body: Multiply paid quantity by unit cost price; free units add no purchase cost.

steps.title: Find total selling revenue
steps.body: Add paid and free quantities, then multiply by unit selling price.

steps.title: Calculate the overall rate
steps.body: Compare total revenue with acquisition cost on the acquisition-cost base.

explanation.conclusion: The combined comparison gives the true profit or loss percentage from the promotion.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not assign the listed unit cost to free units when calculating what the buyer actually paid.

PNL-QL-076.difficultyRationale: Two linked calculations are required, but the reasoning path is directly visible.

blocks.content: The book distributor divides book bundles into the groups shown below.

stem.prompt: Calculate the overall percentage gain or loss.

explanation.opening: The groups are quoted by profit or loss rate, so each rate must first be applied to that group's own cost base.
explanation.concept: A group with a larger quantity-by-cost value contributes more to the final result than a smaller group with the same percentage.

steps.title: Find every group cost
steps.body: Multiply each group quantity by its unit cost price.

steps.title: Convert each rate into receipt
steps.body: Apply the stated profit or loss multiplier to that group's cost total.

steps.title: Form the weighted overall rate
steps.body: Add group receipts, compare with combined group cost, and measure the difference on combined cost.

explanation.conclusion: The weighted money comparison gives the overall profit or loss percentage.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not average the displayed rates unless the group cost totals are exactly equal.

PNL-QL-077.difficultyRationale: Two linked calculations are required, but the reasoning path is directly visible.

blocks.content: The remaining {unknownQuantity} units cost ₹{unknownUnitCostPrice} each and will be sold at an unknown {unknownDirection} rate.

stem.prompt: Find the unknown rate needed for an overall {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}.

explanation.opening: The unknown group's rate must make the combined inventory reach a stated overall target.
explanation.concept: Translate the target into a required total selling amount, subtract the selling amounts already fixed, and compare the remaining requirement with the unknown group's cost.

steps.title: Find the target total selling amount
steps.body: Apply the target commercial factor to the total cost of all groups.

steps.title: Remove known group receipts
steps.body: Calculate and subtract the selling amounts of groups whose rates are known.

steps.title: Solve the unknown group's rate
steps.body: Compare its required selling amount with its own cost price.

explanation.conclusion: This comparison gives both the direction and percentage required for the unknown group.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not apply the overall target rate directly to the unknown group alone.

PNL-QL-078.difficultyRationale: The unknown is coupled to several constraints, weighted groups, eligibility rules, or data-sufficiency logic.

blocks.content: Additional units cost ₹{unknownUnitCostPrice} each and are sold at {unknownRatePercent}% {unknownDirection}.

stem.prompt: How many additional units are needed for an overall {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}?

explanation.opening: Here the rate on the additional group is known, but its quantity must be chosen to make the full inventory meet the target.
explanation.concept: Write total cost and total selling price as expressions in the unknown quantity, then impose the target overall multiplier.

steps.title: Summarise fixed groups
steps.body: Add their known costs and selling amounts.

steps.title: Write the unknown group's contribution
steps.body: Use quantity times unit cost for cost and apply its rate for selling price.

steps.title: Set the target equation
steps.body: Equate total selling price to target factor times total cost and solve for quantity.

explanation.conclusion: The valid non-negative quantity satisfying the equation is the required group size.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not calculate the quantity from a percentage difference alone without accounting for both added cost and added revenue.

PNL-QL-079.difficultyRationale: The unknown is coupled to several constraints, weighted groups, eligibility rules, or data-sufficiency logic.

blocks.content: A dealer buys {totalQuantity} units at ₹{unitCostPrice} each.

stem.prompt: At what unit price should the remaining stock be sold for an overall {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}?

explanation.opening: Part of the stock is already sold, so the remaining units must recover the exact balance needed for the overall target.
explanation.concept: Compute the target receipt for all units, deduct receipts already earned, and allocate the balance over the unsold quantity.

steps.title: Compute target total receipt
steps.body: Apply the stated overall rate to the cost of the complete inventory.

steps.title: Deduct completed sales
steps.body: Add the receipts from sold groups and subtract them from the target.

steps.title: Find the remaining unit price
steps.body: Divide the outstanding receipt by the number of units still unsold.

explanation.conclusion: This division gives the required selling price per remaining unit.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not apply the target percentage only to the unsold portion; it is an overall inventory target.

PNL-QL-080.difficultyRationale: The unknown is coupled to several constraints, weighted groups, eligibility rules, or data-sufficiency logic.

blocks.content: A dealer buys {totalQuantity} units at ₹{unitCostPrice} each.

stem.prompt: At what profit or loss rate should the remaining stock be sold for an overall {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}?

explanation.opening: The remaining stock needs a rate, so first determine its required unit selling price and then compare that price with unit cost.
explanation.concept: This is a two-stage inverse: balance the whole inventory target, then translate the remaining-unit price into profit or loss percentage.

steps.title: Balance the inventory receipt
steps.body: Subtract receipts from units already sold from the target receipt for the full stock.

steps.title: Recover the required unit price
steps.body: Spread the outstanding amount equally across the units still available.

steps.title: Convert price to a rate
steps.body: Compare the recovered unit price with unit cost and measure the difference on unit cost.

explanation.conclusion: The final comparison gives the required profit or loss rate on the remaining units.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not report the outstanding receipt as a percentage before dividing it across the remaining quantity.

PNL-QL-081.difficultyRationale: The unknown is coupled to several constraints, weighted groups, eligibility rules, or data-sufficiency logic.

blocks.content: A produce merchant buys {totalQuantity} crates at ₹{unitCostPrice} each. Of these, {goodQuantity} good crates are sold at ₹{goodUnitSellingPrice} each and {spoiledQuantity} crates are spoiled. The merchant wants an overall {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}.

stem.prompt: Find the recovery required per spoiled crate.

explanation.opening: The good stock produces a known receipt, while the spoiled stock must provide the remaining recovery needed for the target.
explanation.concept: Calculate target total recovery for the whole purchase, subtract revenue from good units, and spread the balance over spoiled units.

steps.title: Find total purchase cost
steps.body: Multiply total quantity by unit cost price.

steps.title: Find the target total recovery
steps.body: Use break-even or the stated overall profit or loss factor.

steps.title: Recover the spoiled-unit requirement
steps.body: Subtract good-unit revenue and divide the remaining amount by spoiled quantity.

explanation.conclusion: The quotient is the minimum or required recovery per spoiled unit.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not measure the target only on the good units; the original cost includes the entire stock.

PNL-QL-082.difficultyRationale: The unknown is coupled to several constraints, weighted groups, eligibility rules, or data-sufficiency logic.

blocks.content: Two articles are sold at the same selling price. One is sold at a profit of {ratePercent}% and the other at an equal loss percentage.

stem.prompt: Find the overall loss percentage.

explanation.opening: Equal profit and loss rates do not cancel when two articles are sold for the same price.
explanation.concept: The common selling price corresponds to two different cost prices, and the higher cost on the loss article creates an unavoidable overall loss.

steps.title: Use a common selling-price base
steps.body: Take the equal selling price as a convenient amount.

steps.title: Recover both costs
steps.body: Divide by 1+r/100 for the profit article and by 1−r/100 for the loss article.

steps.title: Compare combined totals
steps.body: Measure the total shortfall on total cost; the standard result simplifies to r squared divided by 100.

explanation.conclusion: The pair therefore produces an overall loss, not no profit and no loss.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not add the signed rates and conclude zero; their percentage bases are different.
explanation.shortcut: For equal selling prices and equal opposite rates r%, the overall loss is r²/100 percent.

PNL-QL-083.difficultyRationale: A reverse step, base conversion, or two-stage commercial transformation is required.

blocks.content: Two electronic items are sold for the same amount. The first is sold at {knownRatePercent}% {knownDirection}. The second must have a {unknownDirection} result, and the two sales together must produce an overall {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection}.

stem.prompt: Find the required percentage on the second item.

explanation.opening: One article's rate and the combined result are known, so the second cost factor must be recovered from the overall equation.
explanation.concept: Use the common selling price to express both cost prices, then impose the stated total profit or loss condition.

steps.title: Express the known article's cost
steps.body: Reverse its stated commercial multiplier from the common selling price.

steps.title: Represent the unknown cost
steps.body: Write it using an unknown profit or loss multiplier.

steps.title: Apply the combined target
steps.body: Compare twice the common selling price with the sum of both costs and solve the unknown rate.

explanation.conclusion: The rate that satisfies the combined condition is the second article's result.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not use the known rate as though both articles had equal cost price.

blocks.content: The total cost price of a stock is ₹{totalCostPrice}. If the stock is sold at {ratePercent}% {direction},

stem.prompt: Find the total selling price.

explanation.opening: This inventory has already been condensed into one total cost or selling amount, so it behaves like a single commercial transaction.
explanation.concept: Apply the stated overall multiplier in the forward direction, or divide by it when the original total cost is required.

steps.title: Form the overall multiplier
steps.body: Use 1+r/100 for profit and 1−r/100 for loss.

steps.title: Move in the required direction
steps.body: Multiply total cost to get total selling price, or divide total selling price to recover total cost.

explanation.conclusion: The resulting total is the required inventory value.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not apply the rate separately to unknown groups when the question already gives an overall total.

stem.prompt: Find its total cost price.

explanation.opening: This inventory has already been condensed into one total cost or selling amount, so it behaves like a single commercial transaction.

steps.title: Move in the required direction

blocks.content: The total cost of the stock is ₹{totalCostPrice}, and the amount recovered is {recoveredFraction} of that cost.

stem.prompt: Find the overall profit or loss percentage.

explanation.opening: The recovered fraction tells us directly how much of the original inventory cost returned as revenue.
explanation.concept: Compare the recovered fraction with one whole cost: above one means profit, below one means loss, and the gap converts to a percentage.

steps.title: Interpret the fraction
steps.body: Treat total cost as one whole unit and write recovered revenue as the stated fraction.

steps.title: Find the gap from one
steps.body: Subtract the smaller fraction from the larger.

steps.title: Convert the gap to percent
steps.body: Multiply the absolute fractional difference by 100.

explanation.conclusion: The direction and percentage follow from whether recovery exceeds or falls short of total cost.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not calculate the percentage on recovered revenue; total cost remains the standard base.

blocks.content: The inventory analyst records several inventory groups in the table below.

stem.prompt: Calculate the overall percentage gain or loss.

explanation.opening: Read the inventory table row by row and convert each row into a cost total and a selling total.
explanation.concept: The table is a compact ledger: quantity and unit cost establish each row's weight, while the selling condition establishes its recovery.

steps.title: Expand the table rows
steps.body: For each row, calculate quantity times unit cost and then apply its stated selling condition.

steps.title: Add the cost column equivalents
steps.body: Combine the row-level cost totals into the full inventory cost.

steps.title: Compare total recovery
steps.body: Add row recoveries and compare them with total inventory cost to obtain the signed percentage.

explanation.conclusion: The table totals, not the visual average of its rates, determine the overall result.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not give every table row equal weight when their quantities or unit costs differ.

blocks.question: Can the required unit selling price of the remaining stock for an overall {targetRatePercent}% {targetDirection} be determined?

stem.prompt: Decide whether either statement alone or both together are sufficient.

explanation.opening: Test each statement independently against the information needed to price the remaining stock.
explanation.concept: A sufficient statement must identify total purchase cost, receipt from units already sold, remaining quantity, and the overall target stated in the question.

steps.title: Check Statement I alone
steps.body: Decide whether it supplies both the purchase details and completed-sale details needed for the inventory balance.

steps.title: Check Statement II alone
steps.body: Apply the same sufficiency test without borrowing any fact from Statement I.

steps.title: Combine only if necessary
steps.body: Use both statements together only when each supplies a different missing part of the required ledger.

explanation.conclusion: The standard data-sufficiency option follows from those two independent checks.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not calculate with facts from both statements while testing whether one statement is sufficient by itself.

blocks.content: The bulk trader purchases and sells several groups of purchase lots.

stem.prompt: Find the overall profit or loss amount.

explanation.opening: This question asks for the overall rupee result, so only the two combined money totals are needed.
explanation.concept: After total cost and total receipt are found, their absolute difference is the required amount; no percentage conversion is necessary.

steps.title: Calculate total purchase outlay
steps.body: Add quantity times unit cost across all purchase lots.

steps.title: Calculate total sales receipt
steps.body: Add quantity times unit selling price across the same lots.

steps.title: Take the signed money difference
steps.body: Receipt above cost is profit; receipt below cost is loss.

explanation.conclusion: The direction and rupee difference together form the requested overall amount.
explanation.commonTrap: Do not divide by total cost when the question asks for an amount rather than a percentage.
